answer: Identities that wander across many wallets still face the same per-identity cost, so splitting into fakes multiplies collateral rather than diluting it. Sybil resistance comes from staking a scarce resource: each agent must lock an opal-bonded deposit before voting or claiming rewards. Slashing on proven duplication makes each extra identity a net loss. Over a long horizon, honest agents recover their stake while attackers burn capital, so forgery stays unprofitable and the registry stays clean. In practice, sa0014 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
